title: Optimize console & econ walkthrough — batching + prefix/KV strategy (PoppyHealth)

Agreed to run a 2-week sandbox sim and share cost spreadsheet + security doc. Next steps: SE to run workload sim, customer to share sample traffic profile.

transcript:
Header: 2027-07-09 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~58m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO PoppyHealth), Mina (Lead ML Eng), Diego (Infra), Rae (PM)

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we want to walk through the Optimize console cost sim, show batching + prefix/KV recs for your customer chat flows, and map to your latency budget. feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Priya: thanks alex. our main goal — reduce inference cost by ~40% without breaking interactive latency for our triage clinicians. p50 needs to stay under ~120ms, p95 under 300ms if possible.
[00:31] Jordan (SE): got it. couple clarifying q's before we jump in, what's your current stack for serving? are you on-hosted or self-hosted?
[00:40] Mina: we're primarily on a managed endpoint from CloudModelEndpoints for now, small on-prem for PHI-sensitive sessions. traffic: bursty during morning shift, average session length about 60 tokens per request, but prompt prefixes for session history average 220 tokens.
[00:57] Alex: perfect, that's helpful. quick note — the Optimize console will simulate both prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching. we'll show two baseline sims: (A) current no-prefetch / small-batch, (B) prefetch + KV + 8-16 batching.
[01:10] Rae (PM): can you define 'prefetch' vs 'KV cache' for us? sometimes the terms blur when we talk inside.
[01:18] Jordan: sure — prefetch here means proactively loading the key/value cache for an active session so subsequent token generation avoids recomputing early layers; KV cache is the actual sequence state stored per session. prefix caching is storing reuseable decoded representations of repeated prefixes, e.g., system prompts or onboarding text. pre-fetching warms that cache before the next user request.
[01:45] Diego: sounds great. any risk with memory blowup if we keep many sessions' KV cache?
[01:50] Jordan: yes, memory is the tradeoff. Optimize suggests TTLs and eviction policies. for Poppy's traffic, we recommend: TTL 22 minutes for active sessions, per-GPU session cap of ~1.5k small-X sequences, and offload cold sessions to object-store-backed compressed KV to reduce memory pressure.
[02:09] Priya: when you say "offload" — does that add latency on cold reads?
[02:12] Jordan: yes, cold reads will add ~10-40ms depending on the storage path in our sim. we route cold reads to cheaper variants when latency budget allows.
[02:21] Alex: okay let's open the console — I'm sharing the deck and cost sheet in chat. (link posted)
[02:30] Jordan: starting the econ sim: baseline assumptions — model: open-m-13b-ish profile, hosted token cost base 0.0009 per token for generation and 0.0002 for input tokens (these are sim numbers to compare scenarios), average request tokens: input 220 (prefix) + 60 user = 280 tokens, generation length 60 tokens; concurrency profile: 120 concurrent users at peak.
[03:02] Mina: that input token count includes session history; often we truncate, but curious what happens if we cache prefixes.
[03:09] Jordan: scenario 1 (no cache): average cost per request ~ (280*0.0002 + 60*0.0009) = calc in sheet ~ $0.067/request. scenario 2 (prefix+KV prefetch): after prefetch, input effective tokens for recompute drop to 40, so cost ~ (40*0.0002 + 60*0.0009) = ~$0.046/request. that's ~32% savings per request at similar p50 if we maintain warm cache.
[03:45] Priya: 32% is good — but what's the extra infra cost for keeping KV warm?
[03:50] Jordan: metric in sim: cache memory footprint adds about 18% more reserved GPU memory cost at peak, but overall cost per million tokens drops ~27% because generation dominates. the console shows break-even in ~7 days for steady traffic.
[04:10] Rae: what about batching effects? we need interactive latency so we can't just queue up big batches.
[04:16] Jordan: right. Optimize recommends dynamic batching heuristics that respect a latency budget. for P50 120ms, we suggest small-window batching with upper-bound batch size 8 for live traffic and burst batching up to 24 for background tasks. in the sim, dynamic batching reduced per-token latency variance and saved ~10%-15% in token cost on top of caching.
[04:42] Priya: can you explain variance? we care a lot about p95/p99 too.
[04:45] Jordan: variance comes from heterogeneous request sizes and scheduling. batching averages compute across requests but can add queuing delay. the Optimize console sim shows queuing only when concurrency spikes above configured threshold. you can add latency SLO rules to force immediate dispatch if queueing exceeds 30ms.
[05:05] Mina: any model-level tricks? quantization or smaller model variants for cold paths?
[05:09] Alex: yep — routing to cheaper model variants is a staple. route short/cold sessions to a 6B-quantized variant for initial responses, then promote to 13B if quality drift is detected. fallback policy is automatic in the console: if generated quality metric drops, switch back.
[05:27] Diego: quality metric — how are you measuring it in the sim?
[05:30] Jordan: we use a combination of perplexity delta and a small set of reference prompts (we can add your own eval set). in the sim we penalize routes that increase perplexity beyond 12% and include a manual review flag.
[05:45] Priya: okay let's look at a concrete timeline — show me the 2-week sandbox results you propose.
[05:50] Jordan: step 1: ingest a 7-day trace you provide; step 2: run two sims — one with TTL 22m prefetch + batch cap 8, another with TTL 60m + batch cap 16, and a control. we'll output per-route cost, memory pressure, and p50/p95 latencies. step 3: we run a short canary for 24-48h on a subset of users.
[06:20] Rae: what about regulatory constraints — some sessions are PHI and must stay in private infra. can we mix hosted and dedicated?
[06:27] Alex: yes, Redwood supports hybrid routing: PHI-tagged sessions can route to Dedicated or Private nodes, others to Hosted. Optimize shows per-route billing and capacity planning. you'll get separate estimates for Dedicated monthly commit vs hosted per-token.
[06:42] Priya: curious about encryption — KMS/HSM?
[06:44] Alex: we support KMS; Private deployments can use HSM integrations. I'll include the security pack in the follow-up.
[06:52] Mina: can we see an example cost delta for a mixed route: 20% PHI in dedicated, 80% hosted, with prefetch enabled only for hosted?
[06:58] Jordan: quick on-the-fly sim — in sheet scenario "hybrid-prefetch": overall cost per request ~ $0.052; dedicated portion increases fixed monthly cost but per-token compute is slightly lower for committed capacity. net savings with prefetch are still ~25% vs no-cache baseline. I'll put the details in the sheet.
[07:24] Priya: there's often concern about cache warming latency — if a clinician opens a new session, how long before the KV is useful?
[07:30] Jordan: depends. if the session has repeated boilerplate (e.g., intake form), you can prefetch at session start in the client or as a background prefetch. that can be <50ms if local warm, or 100-200ms if you need to fetch from a warm object-store. but the tradeoff is increased memory usage.
[07:49] Rae: what about eviction policies — LRU vs TTL vs LFU?
[07:53] Jordan: we recommend TTL+LRU hybrid for your profile — TTL to keep active sessions and LRU to reclaim for long tails. Optimize lets you simulate different policies and shows memory churn.
[08:08] Diego: any integration complexity? our infra is kubernetes on cloud + s3-like object store.
[08:12] Alex: that's supported. we'll provide a deployment guide. we also support offloading compressed KV to object store with async prefetch to the node. integration is mostly config and a small agent to tag PHI sessions.
[08:24] Priya: what's the expected engineering lift for the prefetch client changes?
[08:27] Jordan: typically a couple of small client changes: add a prefetch call on session start, add session IDs for KV association, and a server-side TTL config. estimate 2-3 dev-weeks with testing. Mina: that's acceptable.
[08:40] Mina: any examples of other customers with similar profile?
[08:42] Alex: we ran a similar sim with 'Harbor-Tech' — they saw ~29% savings with TTL 20m and batch cap 10. but every workload differs; that's why the sim matters.
[08:55] Priya: competition? we heard VertigoAI has a built-in session cache; how does Redwood differ?
[08:59] Jordan: VertigoAI's approach is more blackbox — Redwood exposes the cache controls, eviction policy, and end-to-end cost sim in the Optimize console. we also provide clear routing policies and can mix Dedicated/Hosted.
[09:13] Rae: let's talk SLA/availability — if we depend on warm KV, how do we keep availability?
[09:17] Alex: we design fallbacks: if KV miss occurs, we still serve from model but at higher cost/latency. automatic fallback policies route to an alternate region or model variant. Our Dedicated offering also has burst capacity to avoid outages.
[09:30] Mina: earlier you mentioned a 7-day break-even — can you repeat that calc?
[09:33] Jordan: in sim with your traffic: incremental memory/gpu cost adds $X/day (sheet shows $1,200/day), while token savings accrue $Y/day (~$1,700/day), so net positive after ~6-8 days. I'll include the exact line items in the sheet.
[09:52] Priya: great. one last technical q — how deterministic is tokenization across model variants? we saw odd differences that affected counts.
[09:58] Jordan: tokenization can vary; Optimize has a tokenization profiler to compare counts across variants. we recommend normalizing by selecting a canonical tokenizer for accounting, and the sim can run both to show variance.
[10:12] Rae: OK summarizing next steps — Poppy to send 7-day trace; Redwood to run sim and share sheet; SE to annotate recommendations and run a 24-48h canary after alignment. Alex to send security + pricing.
[10:28] Alex: perfect. anything else?
[10:32] Priya: please include an explicit recommended config we can copy into our infra as a starting point.
[10:36] Jordan: yes we'll provide a one-click config snippet (runtime flags: batch_cap=8, latency_slo_ms=120, kv_ttl_mins=22, route_policy=hybrid-prefetch).
[10:46] Priya: thanks — this was super helpful.
[10:49] Alex: thanks all — we'll follow up in chat with the artifacts.
[10:53] (crosstalk) Diego: quick thing — can you annotate the sheet with expected memory per-session?
[10:56] Jordan: yes - adding that now to the sheet.
[11:02] End of call.
